quotes_checked: 28 of 28 exact (4 agreed, 8 per reading); 1 Corinthians 10:2 also fetched for a proposed addition

fixes.why: 'Christians agree that Christ commanded it' and 'Every reading below takes the text to say that Christ's followers are baptized in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit' are stated of all Christians. Quaker and Salvation Army practice has no water baptism, and Oneness Pentecostal bodies baptize in the name of Jesus (Acts 2:38 on this very card). The writer's own _why flags this. A scholar of religion would call the universal claim inaccurate even though the card's readings all hold it.
fixes.fix: Intro: 'Among the churches whose readings are set out here, all agree that Christ commanded it, and they read the text differently on...'. agreed.summary: 'Every reading below takes the text to say that...' (unchanged) preceded by nothing further, but add at the end: 'A few bodies, such as the Quakers and the Salvation Army, do not practise water baptism, and some Oneness Pentecostal bodies baptize in the name of Jesus alone; this page does not set out their readings.'

fixes.where: reading 2 passages: Genesis 17:7 and Genesis 17:12 notes
fixes.why: The notes state what the Genesis verses say, which is fine, but the card places them under a reading about baptism without saying that the link to baptism is the holders' typological reading (via Colossians 2:11-12), not something Genesis says. Only Genesis 17:12 is purely about circumcision of males at eight days; the Old Testament is not quoted as speaking of baptism.
fixes.fix: Genesis 17:7 note: 'In Genesis the covenant is made with Abraham and his descendants; holders of this reading take baptism to be the sign of that same covenant.' Genesis 17:12 note: 'In Genesis the sign, circumcision, is given to infant males and to those born in the household; holders of this reading take baptism to stand where circumcision stood.'

fixes.why: The strongest typological verse in the covenant reading is missing. Covenant-sign holders cite Israel passing through the sea as a baptism that included the whole people with their children (1 Corinthians 10:2, with 1 Peter 3:20-21 on the flood). Without a verse where the New Testament itself calls an Old Testament event a baptism, the reading's biblical-theological spine (Genesis 17, Colossians 2) is thinner than the other two readings' direct baptism texts. Swap with Acts 16:15 or Romans 4:11 if the count of 8 must hold, or allow 9.
fixes.fix: Add: {"ref": "1 Corinthians 10:2", "quote": "They were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.", "note": "Read as the New Testament naming the crossing of the sea, which included Israel's children, a baptism."}

fixes.why: The label states 'a public sign of grace already received' as the reading of all three traditions, but the summary says Pentecostal members differ on what water baptism gives and Anabaptist members differ on how it relates to grace. The label is firmer than the summary.
fixes.fix: Label: 'Baptism of those who believe: obedience to Christ's command and a public answer to the gospel'.

fixes.where: reading 1 summary and Mark 16:16 / John 3:5 notes
fixes.why: John 3:5 is read by many (including some who hold reading 1) of the Spirit's work, and by other readings as not about baptism; the note 'Read as naming baptism together with the Spirit' is accurate as the holders' reading, but the card elsewhere marks textual disputes (Mark 16:16). A short note that 'water' in John 3:5 is itself debated would keep the card consistent; likewise Acts 16:34 (Berean 'and all his household rejoiced') should be cited in reading 3 if its answers rely on it, since the quoted Berean wording is what a reader can check.
fixes.fix: John 3:5 note: 'Read as naming baptism together with the Spirit in new birth; other readers take "water" otherwise.' Optionally add Acts 16:34 to reading 3 passages with the Berean text read from /api/verse.

summary: All 28 quotes are the Berean's exact words, no verdict words appear, and each reading is stated in its holders' terms with balanced verse counts. The card needs its universal 'Christians agree' claims narrowed to the churches it covers, its Genesis notes framed as the holders' typology, the Exodus-baptism verse added to the covenant reading, and the third label brought in line with its own summary.
